tool.name: Samplot VCF
tool.description: plot every structural variant in a VCF
tool.command:
#import re #if str($sample_ids.source) == 'names' #set $sample_names = [re.sub(r'\.(bam|cram)$', '', str(a.element_identifier)) for a in $alignments] ## samplot keys a dict on these, so a repeated name would silently drop a sample #if len(set($sample_names)) != len($sample_names) echo 'Dataset names must be unique once a trailing .bam or .cram is removed' >&2 && exit 1 && #end if #end if @LINK_ALIGNMENTS@ ln -s '$vcf' input.vcf && #if $filters.important_regions ## samplot reads every line as chrom/start/end, so drop headers and blank lines awk 'NF >= 3 && !/^[#]/ && !/^(track|browser)([ \t]|$)/' '$filters.important_regions' > regions.bed && #end if
samplot vcf --vcf input.vcf --out-dir samplot-out --output_type '$output_type' --bams #for $aln in $staged_alignments '$aln' #end for #if str($sample_ids.source) == 'names' --sample_ids #for $name in $sample_names '${name.replace("'", "'\\''")}' #end for #end if $filters.plot_all --min_bp $filters.min_bp #if str($filters.max_mb) --max_mb $filters.max_mb #end if #if str($filters.min_call_rate) --min_call_rate $filters.min_call_rate #end if #if str($filters.max_hets) --max_hets $filters.max_hets #end if --min_entries $filters.min_entries --max_entries $filters.max_entries #if $filters.important_regions --important_regions regions.bed #end if ## an empty value turns the title fields off; leaving the flag out would restore the default --format '$format' --downsample $downsample ## anything samplot vcf does not recognise is passed on to every samplot plot call @REFERENCE_ARG@ --manual_run --command_file samplot_commands.txt && python '$__tool_directory__/run_samplot_commands.py' samplot_commands.txt samplot-out && cp samplot-out/index.html '$index' && mkdir -p '$index.files_path' && find samplot-out -maxdepth 1 -name '*.${output_type}' -exec cp {} '$index.files_path' ';'

param.label: Structural variant calls
param.help: VCF with SVTYPE (and END) in the INFO column and one genotype column per sample.

param.name: source
param.label: Match alignment files to VCF samples by
param.help: samplot needs to know which alignment file belongs to which VCF sample column.
param.option: Read group sample name (SM tag) in each alignment file
Dataset names (a trailing .bam or .cram is dropped)

param.label: Plot all variants and samples
param.help: By default only variants with at least one non-reference genotype are plotted, with the carriers plus some reference samples as controls.

param.label: Maximum SV length (Mb)
param.help: Skip variants longer than this. No limit by default.

param.label: Minimum call rate
param.help: Only plot variants called in at least this fraction of samples.

param.label: Maximum number of heterozygous samples
param.help: Skip common variants carried by more samples than this.

param.label: Minimum samples per plot
param.help: Add reference-genotype samples as controls until each plot has this many panels.

param.label: Regions of interest
param.help: Only plot variants that overlap these BED regions.

param.label: FORMAT fields in panel titles
param.help: Comma-separated FORMAT fields to show next to each sample name. Clear it to show sample names only.

param.label: Normal pairs to plot
param.help: Number of concordant read pairs to draw per sample.

tool.help:
## What it does
Runs `samplot vcf`: for every structural variant (SV) in a VCF that passes the selection filters, samplot draws a plot of the alignment evidence (read depth, discordant pairs, split reads) for the samples that carry it, plus some reference-genotype samples as controls. This is the quick way to review a whole call set by eye.
## Inputs
- **Structural variant calls**: a VCF with `SVTYPE` and `END` in the INFO column (as written by Manta, Lumpy/smoove, Delly, TIDDIT and most other SV callers) and one genotype column per sample. - **Alignment files**: one BAM or CRAM per sample. samplot matches them to the VCF sample columns either by the `SM` tag of the read group in each file, or by the dataset names (handy with a collection whose element names are the sample names). - **Reference genome**: only needed for CRAM input.
### Matching by dataset name
Each dataset name (minus a trailing `.bam` or `.cram`) must match a VCF sample column exactly.
- Alignments whose name has no matching column are not plotted. - Two alignments with the same name are rejected. - Galaxy replaces unusual characters in dataset names (for example `~`) with `X` before the tool sees them, so use read group matching for samples with such names.
### Unusual names in the VCF
samplot passes sample names, chromosome names and SV types on to its plotting step separated by spaces.
- A sample name containing a space loses its panel title. - If one of these values would be read as an extra samplot option (it starts with a dash, or has a space followed by a dash), the job stops with a `Refusing to run a samplot plot command` error instead of plotting.
## Outputs
- **Plots**: a collection with one image per plotted variant, named `<SVTYPE>_<chrom>_<start>_<end>`. - **HTML index**: samplot's interactive table of the plotted variants, with the images stored alongside it. The page loads its scripts from public CDNs, so it only works when the Galaxy server lets this tool's HTML through unsanitized; otherwise use the plot collection.
## Variant selection
Without *Plot all variants and samples*, only variants with at least one non-reference genotype are drawn. Each plot shows up to *Maximum carriers per plot* carriers, padded with reference samples up to *Minimum samples per plot*. Use the length, call-rate and region filters to focus on the variants you care about.
samplot 1.3.0 does not draw translocations from a VCF: BND and TRA records are skipped or drawn as a single interval. Plot those with **Samplot plot**, which takes both breakpoints.
For more detail see the [samplot documentation](https://github.com/ryanlayer/samplot).
